memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When the trumpets sounded, the army shouted, and at the sound of the trumpet, when the men gave a loud shout, the wall collapsed; so everyone charged straight in, and they took the city. — Josh 6:20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
And there it is — the moment everything had been building toward. The trumpets sound, the people shout, and the mighty walls of Jericho simply collapse. Not breached by battering rams, not tunnelled under, not scaled by ladders. They fell flat, all at once, by the power of God. What no army could have accomplished, God did through the obedience of a people willing to march and shout at His command.

Notice the order of events. The people obeyed fully — all the marching, all the silence, all the waiting — and then the walls fell. The victory came after the obedience, as its fruit. This does not mean their marching had power in itself; the power was entirely God's. But God chose to release His power in response to their faith-filled obedience. Faith and obedience are the channel through which God's power flows.

The New Testament remembers this very moment as a triumph of faith: "By faith the walls of Jericho fell, after the army had marched around them for seven days" (Heb 11:30). It was faith, not military might, that brought down those walls.

What walls are standing in your life today? Walls of fear, of stubborn circumstance, of long-standing struggle? The God who flattened Jericho has not lost His power. Through Christ, we are more than conquerors (Rom 8:37). Our task is to keep trusting and obeying, and to leave the falling of the walls to God, in His perfect time.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What walls in your life are you trusting God to bring down in His time?
2. Do you see obedience as the channel through which God works, even when it feels powerless?
3. How does Jericho's collapse strengthen your confidence in God's power?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, the walls in my life feel immovable, but You brought down Jericho. Help me keep trusting and obeying, and leave the walls in Your mighty hands. Amen.
